strings.name: Kathryn Bigelow
strings.summary: Bigelow moved from visual art into film, examining violence and power through action, horror and political thrillers. Point Break and Strange Days emphasize movement and images; The Hurt Locker and Zero Dark Thirty address war and security. The first woman to win the directing Oscar, she continued with nuclear crisis and decision-making in A House of Dynamite.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: War and action films including The Hurt Locker established her influence; she became the first female directing-Oscar winner.

strings.facts.f2.label: Education and beginnings
strings.facts.f2.value: Worked in visual art before studying film at Columbia.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Directing breakthrough
strings.highlights.h1.text: The Hurt Locker made her the first woman to win the directing Oscar.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Genre and reality
strings.highlights.h2.text: Uses sensory intensity to examine institutions, violence and crisis.
